title: Visit gaps left two-week flowering duration uncertain in 361 of 842 selected US shrub records in 2009-2014
abstract: We tested how well presence and absence reports bound the time from first bloom to end bloom. The public US lilac and honeysuckle archive gave 842 selected plant-years at 231 sites with usable date brackets in 2009-2014. Under correct reports and one ordered flowering episode, 393 records required at least 14 days and 754 allowed at least 14 days. Thus 361 records could fall on either side of this threshold. The mean duration could range from 13.50 to 26.75 days. All four region and period samples had uncertain cases. Adding a full-bloom bracket narrowed the duration range in only one of 802 usable cases. A seven-day visit-gap filter reduced uncertainty but retained a selected subset. These are sharp possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. Unknown report errors, missing endpoints, selected garden plants, and six years of data limit wider use. We do not estimate a climate or pollution effect. Code, source hashes, a modern source extract, tables, formula checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: The visit-based range for the share with duration at least 14 days and for the mean duration. These are possibility bounds for selected records, not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Motivates use of actual visit brackets; our outcome is duration within a plant, not spread among plants.
Historical flowering-duration study; our modern observation-bound audit uses a different period and estimand.
